summary: This was a map new to us, 60% sea. Our three seats (one Opus player) split at 0:05 into a hover platform on the Armada seat and a shipyard on each Cortex seat. The Cortex commanders built winds and a yard and never another extractor, so those two seats ran on 6.3 and 4.2 metal a second from 1:00 to 14:00. Meanwhile a list bug (2:00-3:19) turned the yards' construction ships away from the sea spots, and they were then given to the Armada seat. thebluegecko went navy: Eels from 3:26 shelled us from out of sight and killed the frames at our t2 yard, Dolphin packs raided our undefended sea extractors (16 lost on seat 0), and from 10:00 his Corsairs and Ellysaws outranged our Crocodiles (700 against 370). Our one good fight (F4, 8:53-9:30, 7 Dolphins and 2 Eels killed) was followed by 7 Crocodiles lost into 2 Corsairs at D4 (10:01-10:45), then 13 Possums and single Oppressors fed piecemeal into F5 (12:25-13:35). His Crocodiles raided our land from 13:17 and we surrendered at 15:51; afterwards he said hovers are for harass, not the army's bulk.

root.what: The plan for the sea map gave each seat its own factory on its own economy: the two Cortex commanders got three winds, a shipyard and no extractor step, though a commander is the only builder that reaches all 24 spots. The sea spots were left to construction ships, which a list bug then turned away (2:00-3:19). So two of three seats never had an economy for an army. This is the reader's reading, matching the ledger and other-maps.md. thebluegecko's own reading names the hover seat's army instead (our_mistakes 10:01, 10:45).

our_mistakes.what: The two Cortex seats got three winds and a yard with no commander expansion, and no commander took a sea spot all game. With 6.3 and 4.2 metal a second, each yard finished one 960-metal Oppressor in ten minutes. A stronger plan: the commanders take the near sea spots first, and the seats feed one strong yard. This is the reader's reading; the player wrote the same lesson at 15:51.

bears_on.note: This game is the lesson's source. The hover seat made 13 Crocodiles, 13 Possums and 3 Seekers. After 8:00 no hover went west of x=2048, and the Crocodiles died into Corsairs at D4 (10:01-10:45).
From 10:45 the body was 13 Possums (710 reach), with Crocodiles and single Oppressors as the screen; they lost at F5, 7 Possums and 2 Crocodiles for 835.
Three seats' groups arrived one at a time at D4 and F5. The player at 15:51: 'our three seats split into 6+ small groups that arrived one at a time'.
4,451 to 6,389 metal of wrecks were known from 11:00 with nothing at work. The user asked for resurrection subs at 13:28; they were queued at 13:53 and none finished.
Here we were the side with undefended extractors: 15 of the 16 sea extractors lost on seat 0 had no soldier or turret near, and spot_10 and spot_16 went three times each.
Three Seekers crossed 3:00-4:12 and killed 3 construction ships. After 8:00 nothing of ours crossed, and he expanded and built his navy unharassed.
Two of three seats held 2 and 1 extractors all game, and the side peaked at 12 of 24. Whether the loss was the economy alone cannot be told: there is no truth file for his count.
The 10:00 window (seat 0: 1,890 against 150 seen) was used, but against a fleet out of sight that outranged the attackers. A lead read from what is seen is not a lead in reach.

tools: ad-hoc reads of the three records (finished events, stores by minute, distance to his base, frame losses), bot.log, script.txt
lens.caveats: No truth file: his economy, army and tier 2 are floors or unknown. The tools' enemy-start guess fell on our own coast (H8, G2, G3 by seat), so minutes.py's 'his half' columns, WINDOWS and 'units sent to his side' are meaningless here; reach to his base (B6, 1284,2700) was recomputed from the records. analyze_match, wake_read and impedance_sweep read record-0 only; seats 1 and 2 went through per-seat symlink directories in the scratchpad. The records have no end row. Loss sums from the record count frames at full cost unless said. pro_baseline was not run (not Comet; no cards for this map).

open_questions: How many extractors and how much navy did he have at 8:00 and 10:00? Without a truth file it cannot be told whether we were behind on economy before the fleet fights or level and lost on reach.
Was the bare 'spot_N is not free' skip (the ships' sea spots at 2:00-2:46, commander_t2's land spot_12 at 15:19) ever fixed, and what excluded those spots?
Did the hands hold the Crocodiles about 600 from the Corsairs at 10:20-10:37 by a reach-keeping rule, or does the group centre hide a spread that did close?
Would the Cortex commanders taking the six near sea spots from 0:05 have given the yards an army before his Corsairs came at 10:00?
